description: three-client Stable lobby and multiplayer lifecycle with one packet per action and causal actor/recipient drains

safety.reason: this case creates a live room, sends an invite and synthetic gameplay state, then closes the room

fixture_contract: primary, peer and invitee are unrestricted, unsilenced Stable sessions with clean response queues
primary, peer and invitee identities use the same numeric ids and usernames on both isolated targets
all user and match ids are supplied as JSON integers; each match id is between zero and 63
both room passwords are valid UTF-8 and at most 32 bytes
no multiplayer match exists and stable_mp_match_id is the next free id on both targets
invitee is already subscribed to the real #lobby channel on both targets and its bootstrap queue is drained
the reference invitee reached #lobby through join_lobby followed by channel_join while Zigcho joined it through join_lobby
primary and peer are not in the lobby, a match, a tournament channel or a spectator session before the case
invitee is not in a match, tournament channel or spectator session and remains the lobby observer throughout the room lifecycle
peer joins the first free slot and primary moves from slot zero to slot two before transferring host to peer in slot one
the configured map metadata is an identical logical fixture on both targets
each action is followed by an empty actor poll and every affected recipient is polled before the next mutation can contaminate its queue
blockers: the harness cannot provision three concurrent Stable sessions or pre-join the invitee to #lobby
differential replay therefore requires isolated processes plus externally supplied tokens and mirrored fixture ids
the score frame is deliberately synthetic but conforms to the 29-byte Stable ScoreFrame shape accepted by both parsers
Zigcho drains queued packets before handling a poll while the pinned reference dequeues afterward; action plus immediate actor drain is the causal unit
